title: Bridging FPGA and GPU over PCIe: A Low-Latency Communication Path using AVX-512
problem: Inter-accelerator communication bottlenecks; high latency and complexity in GPU-FPGA bridging
motivation: Need low-latency FPGA-GPU communication for hybrid accelerator systems; DMA overhead limits performance
method: The system uses AVX-512 instructions (the CPU's high-speed data operation set) to directly control data flow over PCIe, rather than relying on DMA hardware controllers. It enables peer-to-peer memory mapping so that GPUs can access each other's memory directly, without data routing through the main CPU. By keeping communication paths short and direct, this design achieves sub-2-microsecond latencies while using simpler software.
key_novelty: Ultra-low sub-2-microsecond latency between GPUs and FPGAs is achieved using AVX-512-driven direct PCIe I/O and peer-to-peer GPU memory mapping, eliminating traditional DMA controllers.
contributions: Programmed I/O mechanism for FPGA-GPU communication
